source_text:
ἀφεῖλεν ὁ θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἀπὸ παντὸς προσώπου.
Ὁ μὲν γὰρ τῶν ὅλων θεός, ἅτε δὴ ζωὴ καὶ ζωοποιὸς ὑπάρχων, ἄφθαρτον ἐπὶ
γῆς ζῷον ἠθέλησεν εἶναι τὸν ἄνθρωπον, εἰ <καὶ> φύσεώς ἐστι φθαρτῆς.
thought_title: God's will for an incorruptible humanity
orientation: Cyril has just quoted Isaiah 25:8 and now begins to explain it by describing God's original intention for the human race.
pass_a_gloss: took away [the] God every tear from every face. [The] [one] indeed for of [the] all God, inasmuch as indeed life and life-giving being, incorruptible upon earth living creature [he] willed to be [the] man, if <even> of nature [he] is of corruptible.

choices.english: an incorruptible living creature on earth
choices.why: Keeps the adjective-noun order and the locative phrase 'on earth' attached to the creature, matching the source word order and the glossary sense of incorruptible.
rejected: a living being on earth that is incorruptible

choices.term: ἅτε δὴ ζωὴ καὶ ζωοποιὸς ὑπάρχων
choices.english: inasmuch as he is life and life-giving
choices.why: Renders the causal participle with 'inasmuch as' to preserve the explanatory force, and uses the glossary terms 'life' and 'life-giving' for the two predicates.
rejected: since he exists as life and giver of life

choices.english: even if he is of a corruptible nature
choices.why: Preserves the concessive force of 'even if' and the genitive of quality 'of a corruptible nature', matching the glossary sense for corruptible.
rejected: even though he has a corruptible nature

choices.term: ἀφεῖλεν ὁ θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἀπὸ παντὸς προσώπου
choices.english: God removed every tear from every face
choices.why: Keeps the aorist indicative as a simple past action and the distributive 'every...every' pattern of the source, matching the Isaiah quotation context.
rejected: God took away every tear from every face
God has removed every tear from every face

bible_refs.note: ἀφεῖλεν ὁ θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἀπὸ παντὸς προσώπου

pass_b_english: God removed every tear from every face (Isaiah 25:8). For the God of all things, inasmuch as he is life and life-giving, willed that the human being should be an incorruptible living creature on earth, even if he is of a corruptible nature.

last_rejected.quote: even if he is of a corruptible nature
last_rejected.why: εἰ καὶ means 'although/even though,' not 'even if'—the Greek states a fact, not a condition.
last_rejected.fix: even though he is of a corruptible nature
last_rejected.ruling: εἰ καὶ can mean 'even if' or 'although'; both convey concession. Not a meaning change.
